whys.why: Why does the audit refuse tracker ids in carve-out names?
whys.because: The audit's name matcher accepts only lowercase slugs, and tracker ids carry uppercase letters.

whys.why: Why does the name matcher accept only lowercase slugs?
whys.because: It was copied from the branch-name validator, which lowercases because git refs fold case on Windows.

whys.why: Why was the matcher copied from the branch-name validator?
whys.because: No shared slug type existed when the audit landed, so each tool wrote its own pattern.

whys.why: Why did no shared slug type exist when the audit landed?
whys.because: The values package that now holds RepoPath was split out two months after the audit.

whys.why: Why was the values package split out after the audit?
whys.because: The split waited on the monorepo move, which left older tools on their own patterns.

whyChain.rootCause: Older tools still carry patterns written before the monorepo move gave them shared value types.
whyChain.rootCheck: `git grep -n slugPattern tools/` today still returns tools/audit/name-matcher.ts:14 and no import from packages/values.
whyChain.readback: Older tools still carry pre-monorepo patterns, therefore the audit never adopted the shared slug type, therefore its matcher copied the branch-name validator's lowercase rule, therefore the audit refuses tracker ids in carve-out names.
